question: What is the main goal of national health sector reform policies?

options.A: To overhaul and strengthen the overall health system
options.B: To completely privatize all public healthcare facilities
options.C: To remove all traditional birth attendants from practice
options.D: To reduce the salaries of healthcare workers in rural areas

explanation: Health sector reforms are structured government strategies created to fix systemic weaknesses and improve overall health outcomes for the population. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T1#BMP322_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why is it helpful for Nigerian midwives to understand national health policies?

options.A: It exempts them from clinical documentation and record keeping
options.B: It connects their daily clinical work to broader public health improvements
options.C: It allows them to write new national healthcare laws independently
options.D: It replaces the need for hands-on midwifery clinical training

explanation: Knowing national policies helps midwives see how their day-to-day patient care fits into national goals for lowering maternal and child mortality. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T1#BMP322_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which of these is a key focus of recent Nigerian health reforms?

options.A: Centralizing all health facility management under the federal capital
options.B: Revitalizing primary health care centres across local government areas
options.C: Banning traditional medicine entirely across all rural communities
options.D: Replacing all hospital doctors with community health extension workers

explanation: Recent policy reforms focus heavily on making primary health care centres functional at the grassroots level where most rural mothers seek care. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T1#BMP322_U2_T1_h2)

question: What has been a common challenge in Nigeria's health sector reforms?

options.A: Gaps between policy creation and actual facility implementation
options.B: Zero interest from international development partners
options.C: Excessive funding that health facilities are unable to spend
options.D: A complete lack of any written healthcare policy documents

explanation: While Nigeria often produces good policy documents on paper, turning those plans into functional services at the clinic level is frequently delayed or stalled. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T1#BMP322_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which indicator is a primary maternal health target in national strategic frameworks?
explanation: National health frameworks measure maternal health success primarily by tracking and aiming to lower the maternal mortality ratio. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T1#BMP322_U2_T1_h3)

question: How does a midwife's daily clinical work directly affect national maternal health targets?

options.A: By providing skilled attendance and essential care during birth
options.B: By writing new federal health bills for the national assembly
options.C: By managing the financial accounts of the Federal Ministry of Health
options.D: By importing medical equipment directly from international manufacturers

explanation: National targets are made up of individual clinical encounters. Skilled birth attendance by midwives directly prevents maternal complications and deaths. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T1#BMP322_U2_T1_h3)

question: Which specific Sustainable Development Goal focuses on health and well-being?
explanation: Sustainable Development Goal 3 is dedicated explicitly to ensuring healthy lives and promoting well-being for people of all ages. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T1#BMP322_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why is it important for national health policies to align with global SDGs?

options.A: It completely removes the need for local government funding of health
options.B: It allows health workers to practice without any professional licensing
options.C: It shifts all healthcare responsibilities away from the federal government
options.D: It helps secure international partnerships, funding, and accountability

explanation: Global alignment reassures international stakeholders and donors, making it easier to mobilize resources and maintain standards for maternal health. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T1#BMP322_U2_T1_h4)

question: What is a major problem with relying solely on out-of-pocket spending for maternity care?

options.A: It forces the government to stop collecting health data entirely
options.B: It creates an excess of cash reserves in primary health clinics
options.C: It automatically eliminates all risks of postpartum hemorrhage
options.D: It deters poor pregnant women from accessing timely care

explanation: When patients must pay cash immediately for every service or drug, many impoverished pregnant women delay or avoid visiting health facilities until emergencies arise. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T1#BMP322_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of the Basic Health Care Provision Fund in Nigeria?

options.A: To purchase luxury vehicles for local government health directors
options.B: To provide international travel allowances for senior health ministers
options.C: To strengthen primary healthcare delivery and protect vulnerable groups
options.D: To fund private specialist hospitals exclusively in major cities

explanation: The BHCPF is designed to channel financial resources down to primary health care facilities to ensure basic services reach mothers and children. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T1#BMP322_U2_T1_h5)

question: How do midwives primarily participate in national health policy implementation?

options.A: By auditing the financial accounts of the national treasury department
options.B: By drafting federal legislation within the national legislative assembly
options.C: By putting evidence-based protocols and guidelines into practice at the facility level
options.D: By managing international trade agreements for pharmaceutical imports

explanation: Midwives are direct implementers of health policies, turning national guidelines into bedside clinical care for pregnant women. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T1#BMP322_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why is accurate data recording by midwives vital for national health sector policies?

options.A: It replaces the need for clinical supervision during labour and delivery
options.B: It prevents patients from ever experiencing any pregnancy complications
options.C: It is only used to determine the monthly salary of hospital accountants
options.D: It provides reliable statistics needed for future health planning and funding

explanation: Accurate facility records feed into the national health information system, enabling policymakers to see real health trends and allocate resources appropriately. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T1#BMP322_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of monitoring and evaluation in health sector reforms?

options.A: To find reasons to dismiss healthcare workers from public service
options.B: To track whether policies are achieving their intended health targets
options.C: To increase the cost of maternal drugs in government pharmacies
options.D: To eliminate the need for community participation in health

explanation: Monitoring and evaluation systems measure progress, identify challenges, and guide necessary corrections to ensure health policies reach their goals. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T1#BMP322_U2_T1_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to maternal health policy success in Nigeria?

options.A: Inadequate health infrastructure and unreliable electricity supply
options.B: Severe stockouts of essential life-saving obstetric medications
options.C: A surplus of highly skilled midwives in remote rural villages
options.D: Financial constraints and high levels of out-of-pocket spending

explanation: Rural areas actually suffer from a shortage of skilled midwives, making a surplus factually incorrect as a barrier. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T1#BMP322_U2_T1_h7)
